# Stripe Provider

This is an independent, community-maintained provider. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by Stripe, Inc.

The Stripe provider manages the objects in a Stripe account: products, prices, customers, coupons, webhook endpoints, tax rates and more. Data sources read objects, and Stripe's read-only catalogues such as country specs and tax codes.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    stripe = {
      source = "computomatic/stripe"
    }
  }
}

# The key comes from the STRIPE_API_KEY environment variable.
provider "stripe" {}
```

## Authentication

The provider authenticates with a Stripe secret key (`sk_live_...` or `sk_test_...`) or a restricted key (`rk_...`). A test-mode key manages your sandbox, and a live-mode key manages your live account. A restricted key needs the permissions of the resources you manage.

Set the key in the `STRIPE_API_KEY` environment variable. The `api_key` argument also takes it, but a key written in a configuration ends up in version control, so prefer the environment variable and never commit a key.

To manage a connected account with the key of its platform, set `stripe_account` to the connected account's ID.

## Live mode and money movement

The resources that move money (`stripe_payment_intent`, `stripe_charge`, `stripe_refund`, `stripe_invoice`, `stripe_credit_note`, `stripe_checkout_session`, `stripe_payout`, `stripe_topup`, `stripe_transfer`, `stripe_transfer_reversal` and `stripe_application_fee_refund`, and `stripe_climate_order`, whose create spends the account's balance) are meant for test data in sandboxes and test mode. Before one creates or changes anything, the provider reads the account's balance and checks Stripe's `livemode` flag. In live mode the change fails at plan time unless the provider block sets `allow_live_money_movement = true`. The key's prefix is never used. A restricted key needs the Balance read permission for this check. Reads, imports and data sources are never checked. The Managing Test Data guide explains how to create, move on and stop managing these objects.

## Stripe API version

Every request is sent with Stripe API version `2026-09-30.endive`. Attributes therefore mean what that version documents, and a change to your account's default API version does not change how the provider behaves. A later provider release may move to a newer API version and says so in its release notes.

## Argument Reference

This provider supports the following arguments:

* `allow_live_money_movement` - (Optional) Allows the resources that move money, such as `stripe_payment_intent` and `stripe_transfer`, to create and change objects in a live-mode Stripe account. Defaults to false: they then work in sandboxes and test mode, and fail at plan time in live mode. The provider asks Stripe for the account's mode; it never infers it from the key.
* `api_key` - (Optional, Sensitive) A Stripe secret or restricted key (`sk_` or `rk_`). Defaults to the `STRIPE_API_KEY` environment variable.
* `base_url` - (Optional) Base URL of the Stripe API, without a path. Defaults to the `STRIPE_API_BASE` environment variable, then `https://api.stripe.com`.
* `files_base_url` - (Optional) Base URL of the Stripe Files API, without a path. Defaults to the `STRIPE_FILES_BASE_URL` environment variable, then `base_url` when that is set, then `https://files.stripe.com`.
* `max_retries` - (Optional) Retries per request on transport errors, 429 and 5xx responses. Defaults to 3.
* `stripe_account` - (Optional) A connected account ID, sent as the `Stripe-Account` header. Defaults to the `STRIPE_ACCOUNT` environment variable.
